nodes.title: Gauss' Law & Electric Flux
points: Electric flux Φ = ∮ E · dA = E A cosθ represents the total number of electric field lines passing normally through a surface. SI unit: N·m²/C or V·m.
Gauss' Law: Total electric flux through any closed Gaussian surface equals 1/ε₀ times the net charge enclosed: Φ = ∮ E · dA = q_enc / ε₀.
Permittivity of free space: ε₀ = 8.854 × 10⁻¹² C²/(N·m²). Dimensions: [M⁻¹L⁻³T⁴I²].
Electric field lines originate from positive charges and terminate at negative charges; they never intersect.
Gauss' law is most useful when the charge distribution possesses high symmetry (spherical, cylindrical, or planar).

nodes.title: Applications of Gauss' Law
points: Infinitely Long Straight Charged Wire (linear charge density λ = q/L): E = λ / (2πε₀r). Field is radial and E ∝ 1/r.
Uniformly Charged Infinite Plane Sheet (surface charge density σ = q/A): E = σ / (2ε₀). Field is uniform, perpendicular to sheet, and independent of distance r.
Conducting Charged Plate: E = σ / ε₀ (twice that of an isolated thin sheet).

Uniformly Charged Thin Spherical Shell (radius R, total charge q): Outside (r > R): E = q / (4πε₀r²); On surface (r = R): E = σ / ε₀ = q / (4πε₀R²); Inside (r < R): E = 0 (charge resides solely on outer surface).

nodes.title: Electric Potential & Potential Gradient
points: Electric potential V is the work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity to that point against electrostatic forces: V = W / q₀. SI unit: Volt (V = J/C).
Potential due to point charge q: V = q / (4πε₀r). Notice V ∝ 1/r (scalar quantity).
Relation between electric field and potential: E = −dV/dr (Electric field is the negative potential gradient). E points in the direction of steepest potential decrease.

Equipotential surface: A surface on which potential is everywhere equal. Work done in moving a charge on an equipotential surface is ZERO (W = q ΔV = 0). Electric field lines are always normal to equipotential surfaces.
Electrostatic potential energy of two point charges: U = q₁q₂ / (4πε₀r).

nodes.title: Electric Dipole & Dipole Interactions
points: Electric dipole moment p = q(2a) directed from −q to +q. SI unit: C·m. Dimensions: [M⁰L¹T¹I¹].
Axial electric field (r ≫ a): E_axis = 2p / (4πε₀r³) (along dipole axis, same direction as p).
Equatorial electric field (r ≫ a): E_eq = p / (4πε₀r³) (anti-parallel to p). Notice E_axis = 2 × E_eq.
Torque on dipole in uniform field: τ = p × E ⟹ τ = pE sinθ. Stable equilibrium at θ = 0°; Unstable at θ = 180°.
Potential energy of dipole in uniform field: U = −p · E = −pE cosθ. Work done in rotating dipole from θ₁ to θ₂: W = pE(cosθ₁ − cosθ₂).

nodes.title: Capacitance & Parallel Plate Capacitor
points: Capacitance C = Q/V: ability of a conductor to store electric charge and potential energy. SI unit: Farad (F = C/V). Dimensions: [M⁻¹L⁻²T⁴I²].
Parallel plate capacitor in vacuum: C₀ = ε₀A / d, where A is plate area and d is separation.
With uniform dielectric of dielectric constant k (or ε_r): C = k C₀ = k ε₀A / d.
With conducting slab of thickness t (t < d): C = ε₀A / (d − t).
With dielectric slab of thickness t and constant k: C = ε₀A / [d − t(1 − 1/k)].

nodes.title: Dielectrics, Polarization & Bound Charges
points: Dielectrics are non-conducting insulating materials that transmit electrostatic effects without conducting charge.
Polar dielectrics (e.g., HCl, H₂O): Centres of positive and negative charges do not coincide; possess permanent dipole moment.
Non-polar dielectrics (e.g., H₂, O₂, CO₂): Centres of positive and negative charges coincide; dipole moment is zero in the absence of external field.
Polarization P: Induced electric dipole moment per unit volume of the dielectric: P = χ_e ε₀ E, where χ_e is electric susceptibility.
Dielectric constant (relative permittivity): k = ε_r = 1 + χ_e = E₀ / E_net = C / C₀.
Reduced electric field inside dielectric: E = E₀ − E_p = E₀ / k, where E_p = σ_p / ε₀ is induced bound charge field.

nodes.title: Combinations of Capacitors (Series & Parallel)
points: Series Combination: Same charge Q on all capacitors; potential divides: V = V₁ + V₂ + V₃.
Equivalent series capacitance: 1/C_s = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + 1/C₃. For two capacitors: C_s = C₁C₂ / (C₁ + C₂). C_s is always less than the smallest individual capacitance.
Parallel Combination: Same potential difference V across all capacitors; charge divides: Q = Q₁ + Q₂ + Q₃.
Equivalent parallel capacitance: C_p = C₁ + C₂ + C₃. C_p is always greater than the largest individual capacitance.
For n identical capacitors of capacitance C: C_p / C_s = n².

nodes.title: Energy Stored in Capacitor & Van de Graaff
points: Electrostatic energy stored in a capacitor: U = ½ CV² = ½ Q²/C = ½ QV.
Energy density (energy stored per unit volume of electric field): u = ½ ε₀ E² (in vacuum) or u = ½ k ε₀ E² (in dielectric).
Sharing of charge between two capacitors: Common potential V_c = (C₁V₁ + C₂V₂) / (C₁ + C₂).
Loss of electrostatic energy during sharing (dissipated as heat/spark): ΔU = [C₁C₂(V₁ − V₂)²] / [2(C₁ + C₂)].

Van de Graaff Generator: Electrostatic machine capable of generating millions of volts (several MV) based on (1) Corona discharge (action of sharp points) and (2) Charge given to a hollow conductor transfers entirely to its outer surface.

formulas.label: Stored energy
formulas.expr: U = ½ CV² = ½ Q²/C = ½ QV

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Dielectric Slab Formulas
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive expression for electric field intensity due to an infinitely long charged wire using Gauss' theorem: E = λ/(2πε₀r).
Board Favourite #2: Derive expression for electric field intensity due to a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet: E = σ/(2ε₀).
Board Favourite #3: Derive expression for capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with a dielectric slab of thickness t: C = ε₀A / [d − t(1 − 1/k)].
Board Favourite #4: Derive expression for energy stored in a charged capacitor U = ½ CV².
Must-Know Definition: Principle of a capacitor (increasing capacitance by bringing an earthed conductor close to an insulated charged conductor).

nodes.title: MHT-CET Battery Reconnection Traps & Droplet Hacks
points: Dielectric Inserted with BATTERY CONNECTED: Voltage V remains constant; C increases by factor k (C = kC₀); Charge increases by factor k (Q = kQ₀); Electric field E = V/d remains constant; Stored energy increases by factor k (U = kU₀).

Dielectric Inserted with BATTERY DISCONNECTED: Charge Q remains constant; C increases by factor k (C = kC₀); Voltage decreases by factor k (V = V₀/k); Electric field decreases by factor k (E = E₀/k); Stored energy decreases by factor k (U = U₀/k).

Coalescence of n Identical Charged Droplets: Radius R = n^(1/3) r; Potential V_big = n^(2/3) V_small; Capacitance C_big = n^(1/3) C_small; Total charge Q_big = n Q_small; Stored energy U_big = n^(5/3) U_small.
Plate Separation Trap: If plate distance d is doubled with battery connected, C halves and energy halves; if disconnected, C halves and energy DOUBLES (external work done against attraction).
